title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Network Analysis Identifies Candidate Kinase-Mediated Thyroid-Associated Targets of Withaferin A.
authors: Abdullah, Ejlal Mohamed; Alameen, Alaa Alnoor; AlAfaleq, Nouf Omar; Alharbi, Mona Shujaa
one_liner_zh: 该文通过转录组与网络分析预测WA相关甲状腺靶点，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心是药物-激酶互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅转录因子富集分析无结合建模，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: Withaferin A (WA), a bioactive steroidal lactone derived from Withania somnifera, has been reported to exhibit diverse pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory effects. Although previous studies suggest a potential link between WA and thyroid-related molecular pathways, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed a comprehensive computational approach to explore WA-responsive molecular changes potentially relevant to thyroid-associated processes. RNA-sequencing data from WA-treated MCF-10A human mammary epithelial cells (GSE158085) were analysed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Because thyroid-specific WA transcriptomic datasets are not currently available, the DEGs were intersected with curated hypothyroidism-associated genes to generate a cross-tissue, exploratory set of candidate genes. The genes that overlapped were used to construct protein-protein interaction networks, prioritize high-centrality candidate genes, and conduct enrichment analyses for transcription factors and kinases. Further analysis of selected upstream kinases was performed using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations with WA. A total of 1458 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified, 10 of which overlapped with hypothyroidism-associated genes. Network analysis identified candidate interactions among the overlapping genes, while higher-confidence analysis retained four connected genes (PTPN22, STAT4, DUOX2, and DUOXA2). Transcription factor enrichment identified ERG, SUZ12, NANOG, TCF3, RUNX1, and TP63 as potential upstream regulators, while kinase enrichment identified candidate upstream kinases associated with the predicted regulatory network. Based on enrichment evidence, structural availability, and literature-supported biological relevance, MAPK14 (p38alpha), AKT1, and MAPK8 (JNK1) were selected for molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Structural analyses suggested potential interactions between WA and the selected kinases, with target-specific dynamic behaviour across the simulated systems. Collectively, the findings highlight WA-responsive genes and predicted gene-TF-kinase relationships that may be relevant to thyroid-associated molecular processes. However, these associations are hypothesis-generating and provide a basis for further investigation in thyroid-derived experimental models.
abstract_zh: Withaferin A (WA) 是一种源自睡茄（Withania somnifera）的生物活性甾体内酯，已有报道显示其具有多种药理活性，包括抗炎和代谢调节作用。尽管先前的研究提示WA与甲状腺相关分子通路之间存在潜在联系，但其潜在分子机制仍未完全阐明。在此，我们采用综合计算方法来探索可能与甲状腺相关过程有关的WA响应性分子变化。分析了WA处理的MCF-10A人乳腺上皮细胞（GSE158085）的RNA测序数据，以鉴定差异表达基因（DEGs）。由于目前缺乏甲状腺特异性的WA转录组数据集，我们将DEGs与精选的甲状腺功能减退相关基因进行交集分析，以生成跨组织的探索性候选基因集。重叠基因用于构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络、优先筛选高中心性候选基因，并进行转录因子和激酶的富集分析。对选定的上游激酶，使用分子对接和分子动力学模拟与WA进行进一步分析。共鉴定出1458个差异表达基因（DEGs），其中10个与甲状腺功能减退相关基因重叠。网络分析识别了重叠基因间的候选相互作用，而高置信度分析保留了四个连接基因（PTPN22、STAT4、DUOX2和DUOXA2）。转录因子富集分析将ERG、SUZ12、NANOG、TCF3、RUNX1和TP63鉴定为潜在上游调控因子，而激酶富集分析则识别了与预测调控网络相关的候选上游激酶。基于富集证据、结构可用性和文献支持的生物学相关性，选择MAPK14（p38alpha）、AKT1和MAPK8（JNK1）进行分子对接和分子动力学模拟。结构分析提示WA与选定激酶之间存在潜在相互作用，且模拟系统表现出靶标特异性动态行为。总体而言，这些发现突出了WA响应性基因及预测的基因-转录因子-激酶关系，这些可能与甲状腺相关分子过程有关。然而，这些关联仅作为假设生成，为在甲状腺来源的实验模型中进行进一步研究提供了基础。
